title: How Much Fiber in Whole Wheat Bread? 1.9g per Slice
description: Whole Wheat Bread: about 1.9 g of fiber per 1 slice (7% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in whole wheat bread?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Bread, whole-wheat, commercially prepared

intro: Whole wheat bread ranks #8 of 8 grains on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in whole wheat bread by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in whole wheat bread?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists bread, whole-wheat, commercially prepared at 6 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 slice; 32 g) therefore has about 1.9 g of fiber and 81 calories. That is 7% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 8% of a 25 g day and 5% of a 38 g day.

Whole wheat bread is an easy daily swap because most people already eat bread. USDA’s generic whole wheat entry gives a couple of grams per slice, about twice white bread. Many packaged breads now go further with added seeds or fiber, and their labels can read 3–5 g per slice.

sections.heading: Reading bread labels
paragraphs: Look for “100% whole wheat” or “whole grain” as the first ingredient. “Wheat bread” or “multigrain” alone does not mean whole grain, and those breads can be close to white bread in fiber.
Slice weight varies widely, from under 30 g for sandwich bread to 45 g or more for dense seeded loaves. Compare grams of fiber per slice on the label rather than assuming every slice is equal.

sections.heading: How whole wheat bread compares with other grains
paragraphs: Of the 8 grains on this site, whole wheat bread ranks #8 for fiber per typical serving and #6 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 2.4 g of fiber per 100 calories, in the middle of the range for the foods on this site.

Close neighbors by serving: [wheat bran](/fiber-in-wheat-bran) at 3.1 g (2 tbsp); [brown rice](/fiber-in-brown-rice) at 3.2 g (1 cup, cooked); [popcorn](/fiber-in-popcorn) at 3.6 g (3 cups, air-popped). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), whole wheat bread is #40 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding whole wheat bread to your day
paragraphs: Two slices of whole wheat toast with peanut butter and a sliced banana make a breakfast in the 8–9 g range. A sandwich on whole-grain bread with hummus and vegetables can pass 10 g.

Example: 2 slices whole wheat bread, 2 tbsp peanut butter, 1 banana. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 8.5 g of fiber, with 3.8 g from the whole wheat bread. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of whole wheat bread?
faqs.a: 6 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Bread, whole-wheat, commercially prepared). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in whole wheat bread (2 slices)?
faqs.a: About 3.8 g, for 64 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Which bread has the most fiber?
faqs.a: Breads with whole grains plus added seeds, bran, or fiber ingredients. Some popular seeded whole-grain loaves list about 5 g per slice. The calculator includes several packaged breads by name, or you can enter the label’s grams.

faqs.q: Is toasting bread a way to lose fiber?
faqs.a: No. Toasting drives off water, so a toasted slice weighs less but keeps essentially the same fiber.
